posts.author_bio: Teaching builders how to extract and use information from documents to make better, faster decisions
posts.post_caption:
Agent history should not become the source of truth for how you work.

A chat captures context-specific off-the-cuff thinking. Automatically extracting every workflow from it to create skills or automations turns temporary decisions and workarounds into a structure creates a lot of process overhead that you then have to deal with on projects.

Use history to get ideas and patterns. Then decide whether each one is good, general enough to reuse, or something you should change in your workflow.

posts.post_caption:
An agent answered with an old refund policy, because the current version was ranked too low to be included in context. The context builder kept only ranks one and two, so the model never saw the current policy. The failure happened in retrieval before generation.

To fix, I would see if historical revisions belong in the corpus at all and remove if not.  Or add a boost to retrieval score based on the date published or updated. I log document ID, rank, source version, and status so I can debug where the problems are in this way.

OCR pipelines and vision-language models can both add text that is not in the image.

I cropped two labels at the right edge: “REQUISITION NUMBE” and “SOLICITATION NUMB.” One model completed both as “NUMBER.” Surya invented an unrelated project-status table. Qwen stopped at the visible labels. With a prompt, Gemini added `[cut off]` only when prompted.

Inferred/Hallucinated  fragments need case-by-case review.

posts.author_bio: Teaching builders how to extract and use information from documents to make better, faster decisions
posts.post_caption:
Agent memory is not one thing. It is a family of retrieval systems.

A project wiki, a conversation with a friend, an X post, and a code snippet should not be stored, chunked, or retrieved the same way. Some need keyword search, some semantic search, and some are fine with grep.

They also need lifecycle rules: what gets stored, updated, deleted, and when it should be retrieved.

A single memory bucket may look fine but it gets cluttered over time.

Design memory like you would a complex retrieval system

#AIAgents #Retrieval #AIArchitecture

An LLM judge is not your eval, it's instrumentation.

The eval is the set of human labels you put on real traces. The judge tries to approximate those labels so you can run them continuously and at scale.

That's why building the judge first makes no sense to me.

posts.post_caption:
A golden dataset gives you a stable place to run experiments, but the goal is not to get to a metric you can just follow.

Early datasets may have 10, 15, 30, or 40 examples. Teams run experiments, hill-climb the metrics, and stop inspecting the underlying cases.

Every metric has blind spot and can be gamed (intentionally or otherwise). After each run, inspect the examples and traces, keep annotating, and do error analysis. 

The score gives you grounding for that review but not replace it.

posts.author_bio: Teaching builders how to extract and use information from documents to make better, faster decisions
posts.post_caption:
Substack will be using Pangram-powered “Scan for AI text” feature for posts.  I hate slop, but I don't think this is the way

I tested Pangram itself and it had similar issues to previous AI detection models. A section divider flipped one sample from 100% human to 100% AI. Adding tiny grammar mistakes moved AI-generated text toward “AI-assisted.”

It worries me that the detector can become the target. Writers may remove useful structure or add mistakes just to look human.

The goal should be better writing, but we should be weary of turning a metric into a target

#AIWriting #Substack #GenerativeAI

posts.post_caption:
Plain text extraction captured every fee and amount, but lost the relationship between each fee, its section, and the subtotal.

Docling rebuilt the tables, then changed the homeowner insurance escrow term from 2 months to 23. A cross-field check caught it: $100.83 × 23 did not equal the extracted escrow total of $202.

Records that fail can go to re-extraction or human review. Then measure field accuracy on a human-labeled set and review a sample of the records that pass.
